See also: Filet

English

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (US) enPR: fĭ'lā, fĭlā', IPA(key): /ˈfɪleɪ/, /fɪˈleɪ/
  • (UK) IPA(key): /ˈfɪlɪt/, /ˈfɪleɪ/
  • Rhymes: -eɪ, -ɪt

Noun

[edit]

filet (plural filets)

  1. (American spelling) Alternative spelling of fillet.

Verb

[edit]

filet (third-person singular simple present filets, present participle fileting, simple past and past participle fileted)

  1. (American spelling) Alternative spelling of fillet.

Anagrams

[edit]
  • flite

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From fil +‎ -et.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central) [fiˈlɛt]
  • IPA(key): (Balearic) [fiˈlət]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [fiˈlet]
  • Audio (Barcelona):(file)

Noun

[edit]

filet m (plural filets)

  1. diminutive of fil (“thread”)
  2. screw thread
    Synonym: rosca
  3. filet (strip of meat or fish)
  4. (architecture) fillet
  5. (typography) line, bar

Derived terms

[edit]
  • filet de faixa
  • filetejar
  • fileteria
  • filetí
  • filetó

Further reading

[edit]
  • “filet”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007
  • “filet”, in Gran Diccionari de la Llengua Catalana, Grup Enciclopèdia Catalana, 2026
  • “filet” in Diccionari normatiu valencià, Acadèmia Valenciana de la Llengua.
  • “filet” in Diccionari català-valencià-balear, Antoni Maria Alcover and Francesc de Borja Moll, 1962.

Dutch

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French filet.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /fiˈleː/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio:(file)
  • Hyphenation: fi‧let
  • Rhymes: -eː

Noun

[edit]

filet m or n (plural filets, diminutive filetje n)

  1. filet (compact piece of meat or fish)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • fileren
  • kalkoenfilet
  • kipfilet
  • zalmfilet

French

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /fi.lɛ/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (France (Agen)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Toulouse)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)

Etymology 1

[edit]

From fil +‎ -et.

Noun

[edit]

filet m (plural filets)

  1. trickle, drizzle (of liquid etc.), wisp (of smoke)
  2. fillet, filet (of meat)
  3. (anatomy) frenulum, frenum
    Synonym: frein
  4. (typography) rule
  5. (architecture) fillet, listel
Derived terms
[edit]
  • coup de filet
  • faux-filet
  • filet à cheveux
  • filet à papillons
  • filet américain
  • filet de pêche
  • filet de sécurité
  • filet japonais
  • filet mignon
  • passer entre les mailles du filet
  • petit filet
  • prendre dans ses filets
Descendants
[edit]
  • → Bulgarian: филе́ (filé)
  • → Danish: filet
  • → Dutch: filet
  • → Finnish: file, filee
  • → German: Filet
  • → Macedonian: филе́ (filé)
  • → Norwegian Bokmål: filet
  • → Norwegian Nynorsk: filet
  • → Persian: فیله
  • → Polish: filet
  • → Portuguese: filete
  • → Russian: филе́ (filé)
  • → Spanish: filete
  • → Ukrainian: філе́ (filé)

Etymology 2

[edit]

Inherited from Old French filé (past participle of filer), with change of suffix.

Noun

[edit]

filet m (plural filets)

  1. (fishing, sports) net
  2. (used for carrying groceries) net
Derived terms
[edit]
  • filet à papillons
Descendants
[edit]
  • → Turkish: file

Further reading

[edit]
  • “filet”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012
